newsitem.title: USA: Argentina wheat plantings seen down 10 pct-attache.
newsitem.headline: Argentina wheat plantings seen down 10 pct-attache.

text.p: Argentina's wheat plantings for 1997/98 will likely be about 10 percent less than last year, an agricultural expert with the U.S. Embassy in Buenos Aires said on Wednesday.

Uncertainties about weather in the coming year has caused some producers to shift from wheat to soybean plantings, Gary Groves, ag counselor with the embassy, said in an interview at the U.S. Agriculture Department headquarters.
"We're showing the wheat area down about 10 percent for next year," Groves said. "But it's too early to think about yields."
Traders have said they expect Argentina's wheat sowings to fall from 11 to 17 percent, and for production to be in the range of 12 to 13 million tonnes.

The Argentine government has forecast production of between 12.5 and 14 million tonnes of wheat for 1997/98. "We're closer to the 14 million tonne production figure," Groves said, referring to USDA figures.
As the agricultural attache with the embassy, Groves contributes information to the USDA but the agency factors in other data before producing official estimates.
In the 1996/97 year, Argentina produced 52 million tonnes of grain. That figure included 14.5 million tonnes of corn, of which about half was exported.
Argentina also produced a record 16 million tonnes of wheat in the 1996/97 crop year, but quality was affected by heavy rains, he said.
Despite drought and rough weather conditions in the past few years, Argentina is well on its way to achieve grains production of 60 million tonnes annually by the year 2000, Groves said.
"If they keep on the road they have, they could reach that goal," he said. "The bulk of that additional production will go to Asian markets."
